review.reason: Read manuscript methods, implemented results, and limitations. Explains incentives; the September 2026 journal text remains unverified.

item.title: Manipulation-Robust Prediction
item.headline: Predict what people will do once they know the rules
item.authors: Daniel Björkegren, Joshua E. Blumenstock, and Samsun Knight
item.summary: In a Nairobi smartphone experiment, anticipating gaming improved predictions under disclosed rules. This reviews the 2025 manuscript; rewards substituted for actual loans.

evidence.question: Can predictions survive people gaming their inputs?
evidence.method: Randomized weekly rewards measured responses; subsequent challenges compared strategy-aware rules with LASSO, a standard regression method.
evidence.limitations: Adult smartphone owners; simple linear rules; analysis required successful weekly participation.

explainer.finding: Anticipating manipulation reduced average prediction error when rules were disclosed.
explainer.method: The app varied incentives and disclosure, measuring payment errors against baseline characteristics.
explainer.meaning: Rewarding call frequency can encourage extra calls without changing income. Predictions must account for that response.
explainer.limits: The income-only advantage was statistically inconclusive. Actual lending and more complex algorithms need separate tests; model assumptions matter.
